meta.title: UK disability issues evidence
meta.note: Figures keep the original area, period, population and definition used by the source. A difference or link in the data does not prove what caused it.

items.title: Employment rate for disabled people
items.detail: About 5.5 million disabled people aged 16 to 64 were in work. The gap between disabled and non-disabled employment rates was 29.7 percentage points.
items.caveat: This covers people aged 16 to 64. The latest year-on-year change was small enough that it may be due to normal survey variation.

items.title: Disability employment gap
items.detail: The difference between the employment rates of disabled and non-disabled people.
items.caveat: The gap shows that the rates are different. It does not tell us, by itself, why they are different.

items.title: Low income after housing costs
items.comparison: 19% where no family member was disabled
items.detail: 21% of people in families with a disabled member were in relative low income after housing costs.
items.caveat: The figures show a link between disability in the family and low income. Other factors may also explain part of the difference.

items.title: Low income before housing costs
items.comparison: 2 percentage points higher than families with no disabled member
items.detail: 17% of people in families with a disabled member were in relative low income before housing costs.
items.caveat: Changes to the disability questions can affect comparisons with earlier years.

items.title: People receiving PIP
items.comparison: 3.4 million working age · 690,000 State Pension age
items.detail: People entitled to Personal Independence Payment (PIP).
items.caveat: This is not a count of all disabled people. It also does not include people receiving Scotland’s Adult Disability Payment.

items.title: Universal Credit health caseload
items.comparison: 78% had limited capability for work and work-related activity
items.detail: People on Universal Credit who have a health condition or disability that limits their ability to work.
items.caveat: This is a benefits figure. It is not a measure of healthcare access or a count of all disabled people.

items.title: Trips made by disabled adults
items.detail: Disabled adults made an average of 713 trips per person in 2025, 21% fewer than non-disabled adults.
items.caveat: The survey shows how often people travelled, but not why the difference exists. It also leaves out people living in care homes and some other communal settings.

items.title: Pupils with an Education, Health and Care plan
items.detail: 538,547 pupils in schools in England had an Education, Health and Care (EHC) plan.
items.caveat: Having an EHC plan is not the same as being counted as disabled in other datasets.

items.title: Pupils receiving SEN support
items.detail: 14.8% of pupils in England received special educational needs (SEN) support.
items.caveat: SEN is a school support category. It should not be used as a direct count of disabled pupils.

items.title: Disability hate crimes recorded by police
items.detail: Police recorded 10,224 disability hate crime offences in England and Wales.
items.caveat: Not every incident is reported to the police. Changes in reporting and recording can also affect the number.

items.title: Taking part in civic life
items.detail: 50% of disabled adults had taken part in civic participation, consultation or activism at least once in the previous 12 months.
items.caveat: Disability status is self-reported. This measures participation, not accessibility or discrimination.

items.title: Renting social housing
items.detail: 24.9% of working-age disabled people rented social housing.
items.caveat: This figure is from 2021, so it should not be presented as a current 2026 estimate.

items.title: Owning a home
items.detail: 39.7% of working-age disabled people owned their home.
items.caveat: This is older survey evidence from 2021 and covers people aged 16 to 64.

items.title: Disability and deprivation at age 40–44
items.detail: 21.6% of people aged 40 to 44 in the most deprived areas of England were disabled, compared with 8.1% in the least deprived areas.
items.caveat: The figures show a link between deprivation and disability. They do not prove that one causes the other.

items.title: Disabled people in Census 2021
items.detail: The share of people classed as disabled using the Census 2021 question and definition.
items.caveat: Census 2021 and the Family Resources Survey use different methods and populations, so the figures should not be compared as if they are the same measure.

items.title: Health and care data
items.comparison: Benefits data is not used as a substitute
items.detail: We do not use Universal Credit health or PIP figures as a substitute for data about healthcare access.
items.caveat: A future health section should use direct data about health services, outcomes or care, with clear definitions of who is included.

items.title: Disabled children: social or behavioural impairment
items.detail: 61% of disabled children were reported as having a social or behavioural impairment.
items.caveat: Children can have more than one impairment. This percentage should not be added to other impairment percentages.

items.title: Working-age disabled adults: mental health impairment
items.detail: 46% of working-age disabled adults were reported as having a mental health impairment.
items.caveat: People can report more than one impairment. This age group should not be directly compared with children or pension-age adults as if they were the same population.

items.title: Disabled pension-age adults: mobility impairment
items.detail: 68% of disabled pension-age adults were reported as having a mobility impairment.
items.caveat: People can report more than one impairment. This age group should not be directly compared with younger groups as if they were the same population.
